messages:
alex: heads-up — we saw sustained queue growth on eu-west-1 around 10:05 UTC, GPUs hit soft-saturation, requests started queuing for >800ms. noticed some customers got dropped to 429s
maria: can you paste the admission-control snapshot? which pool?
alex: pool=rl-inference-prod, priority tiers: gold/silver/beta. active pods 48/48. ingress qdepth spiked to 1200. sending dump:
```
admission_window: 500ms
max_inflight_per_gpu: 16
queue_limit: 1000
spill_policy: cross-region-handshake
```
jamal: 1200 queue is brutal. did the cross-region handoff kick in? logs?
devin: our metric shows handoff attempts to us-east-1 but most were throttled by network egress limit; TCP retries added 150ms. we fell back to model-degraded variant for a subset (gpt-small-quant) to reduce GPU time.
alex: @liz_ops can you confirm whether egress caps were hit or if it’s path-level flapping? cloud console shows egress close to 95% on the eu-west VPC NAT gateway.
liz_ops: confirmed NAT SNAT table saturated — we hit ephemeral port exhaustion on a few nodes. Reducing concurrency on per-node side would help. raised a ticket with cloud provider, but not instant.
maria: can we enable per-customer admission fairness? gold stays prioritized, but limit silver to a lower QPS during region-surge. currently admission is global per-pool.
jamal: proposal: add a windowed handoff that batches cross-region exports every 200ms instead of streaming per-request. reduces egress flows and amortizes TCP connections. patch idea:
```
hand_off_window_ms: 200
max_batch_size: 64
egress_concurrency: 8
```
alex: that would help NAT port exhaustion. also consider short model-fallback thresholds: if queue > 800 && avg_latency > 500ms, route non-gold to model-degraded.
devin: quick config I pushed to canary for 10% of traffic. commit: `cfg:windowed-handoff:v1` — monitoring now. sre-bot: alert policy auto-escalation set for queue_depth > 900.
sre-bot: [auto] canary rollout started for cfg:windowed-handoff:v1 on rl-inference-prod (10% routes).
liz_ops: FYI cost note — cross-region handoff increases egress costs ~1.4x per-token on average. if we fallback to smaller models we save GPU time but might increase total tokens due to verbosity changes. need trade-off analysis.
maria: agree on trade-offs. short-term: keep windowed handoff canary + enforce per-tier qps caps. medium-term: add egress-aware routing that prefers local degraded-model variants before cross-region.
jamal: I'll draft a runbook: steps to flip canary, how to revert, and the exact thresholds. include commands to lower per-node concurrency and to drain NAT-heavy pods.
alex: perfect. put it in eng-infra runbooks and ping #oncall when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
